merger_name: Shepparton Automotive Group - Darryl Twitt Motors dealerships in Shepparton East, Victoria
merger_description:
Jasnic Automotive Pty Ltd trading as Shepparton Automotive Group proposes to acquire the business assets of Goulburn Motor Group (Vic) Pty Ltd trading as Darryl Twitt Motors, by way of a business sale agreement (the **Acquisition**).

Shepparton Automotive Group operates 3 automotive dealerships from a single site located at 80 Benalla Rd, Shepparton. It supplies new vehicles as the authorised representative for Hyundai, Mitsubishi, and Suzuki, and associated vehicle servicing. Shepparton Automotive Group also supplies used vehicles and vehicle financing. Shepparton Automotive Group supplies genuine parts to consumers as part of any scheduled services performed by the dealership.

Darryl Twitt Motors operates 8 dealerships from 2 sites located at 325-329 Midland Highway, Shepparton East and 2-8 Carroll Road, Shepparton East. It supplies new vehicles as the authorised representative for Ford, Honda, Volkswagen, Audi, BYD, Geely, Land Rover, and LDV, and associated vehicle servicing. Darryl Twitt Motors also supplies used vehicles, spare parts, and vehicle financing, as well as servicing for Skoda vehicles.

Darryl Twitt Motors' Land Rover and LDV sales, service, and parts businesses are not included in the Acquisition.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and third-party feedback.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition would be unlikely to have
the effect of substantially lessening competition in any relevant
market. In reaching its decision, and based on the material before it,
the ACCC makes the following findings.
Regarding the supply of new cars:
• SAG would continue to face competition from multiple
alternative suppliers of new cars on an inter-brand basis within
Shepparton, as well as on both an intra-brand and inter-brand
basis in areas surrounding Shepparton.
Regarding the supply of used cars:
• SAG would continue to face competition from multiple
alternative suppliers of used cars.
Regarding the supply of car servicing and repairs and OEM spare
parts:
• SAG and DTM are not close competitors in the supply of car
servicing and repairs and OEM spare parts because they do not
overlap on an intra-brand basis, and dealerships generally
provide these services and parts only for the OEM brands they
supply.
Regarding the supply of automotive finance services;
• SAG would face competition from multiple alternative suppliers
of automotive finance services.
